meta.titre: Germany's Losses at Versailles: land, colonies, army and reparations
meta.sous_theme: What Germany lost in Europe and overseas after 1919, and why war came in 1914
tags: german losses after world war one

sections.contenu_markdown: In Buea and Douala, old buildings and plantations still remind visitors of the years when Cameroon was a German colony called Kamerun. That colony disappeared because Germany lost the First World War and with it all its overseas possessions. Examiners ask what Germany lost and why the war broke out, often in the same essay. This course shows you the losses by category and links them to the long-term causes of the war.

items: The First World War lasted from 1914 to 1918 and was fought between the Allies and the Central Powers.
A colony is a territory ruled by a foreign power.
The League of Nations was an international organisation founded after the war to keep peace.

sections.titre: The Treaty of Versailles and the failure of Bismarck's system
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The treaty

The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919. Germany was not allowed to negotiate and had to accept terms drawn up by the victors, above all Clemenceau of France, Lloyd George of Britain and Wilson of the United States.

### Germany's losses

| Category | Main losses |
|---|---|
| Land in Europe | Alsace and Lorraine returned to France; Eupen and Malmedy to Belgium; North Schleswig to Denmark after a vote; large areas to Poland, which gave Poland access to the sea; Danzig made a free city; the Saar coal region placed under the League of Nations for fifteen years |
| Colonies | All German colonies were taken away and ruled as mandates under the League of Nations |
| Armed forces | An army of no more than 100,000 volunteers; no tanks, no military aircraft, no submarines; a small navy; the Rhineland made a demilitarised zone |
| Money | Germany was made to pay reparations, a sum fixed in 1921 |
| Status | A war guilt clause blamed Germany for the war; union with Austria was forbidden |

### Colonies in Africa and the Pacific

Cameroon (Kamerun) was divided between Britain and France; Togoland was also divided between them. German South West Africa went to South Africa. German East Africa became Tanganyika under Britain, while Rwanda and Burundi went to Belgium. In the Pacific, Australia and New Zealand took German possessions.

### Why the war came: Bismarck's system fails

Bismarck had kept France isolated by alliances, including the Triple Alliance with Austria-Hungary and Italy. He left office in 1890. Without him the German government did not renew the treaty with Russia, so Russia moved towards France and the two allied in the early 1890s. Kaiser Wilhelm II then built a large navy, which alarmed Britain. Britain settled its quarrels with France in 1904 and with Russia in 1907, forming the Triple Entente. Crises over Morocco and the Balkans raised tension, and the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo in June 1914 began the chain of events that led to war.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks 'what losses did Germany suffer' or 'outline the terms of the treaty'
variantes.contenu_markdown: Group the losses into four headings: land, colonies, army and money. Give a fact or two under each heading, and explain the effect of at least two losses. Effects include the loss of coal and industrial areas, resentment among Germans, and the end of German colonial rule in Africa, which is why Cameroon passed to Britain and France.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question links Bismarck, the alliances and the outbreak of war in 1914
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write in time order. Start with Bismarck's alliances, then the non-renewal of the Russian treaty, the Franco-Russian alliance, the naval race, the Entente agreements, the crises, and finally Sarajevo. End by saying that the system of rival alliance blocs turned a local crisis into a general war.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain how the Treaty of Versailles punished Germany in Europe and overseas. [8 marks]

etapes.action: Underline the command word and the two areas.
etapes.justification: 'Explain' asks for effects, not only a list, and the question names two areas: Europe and overseas.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Plan: Europe (land and army) and overseas (colonies), each with a short explanation.

etapes.action: Write the Europe paragraph on land.
etapes.justification: Land losses are among the most important facts and are easy to state precisely.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Germany returned Alsace and Lorraine to France and gave land to Poland, Belgium and Denmark; this reduced its territory and its resources.

etapes.action: Add the army and the money terms.
etapes.justification: These show how the treaty weakened Germany's power and wealth.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The army was limited to 100,000 men with no tanks or military aircraft, and reparations were demanded, so Germany was weak and poor.

etapes.justification: The colonies belong to the 'overseas' part of the question, and Cameroon is a good example.
etapes.resultat_markdown: All colonies were taken and ruled as League mandates; Cameroon was divided between Britain and France.

etapes.justification: A closing sentence shows the overall impact.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Germany lost land, power, wealth and empire, which left many Germans bitter.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: The Treaty of Versailles of 1919 punished Germany heavily. In Europe, Germany had to return Alsace and Lorraine to France and give territory to Poland, Belgium and Denmark, so it lost land and resources, including the Saar coal region, which came under League control. Its army was cut to 100,000 men and it could not have tanks or military aircraft, so it could no longer threaten its neighbours. It also had to pay reparations, which weakened its economy. Overseas, Germany lost all its colonies, which became mandates under the League of Nations. For example, Cameroon was divided between Britain and France. In conclusion, Germany lost land, power, wealth and empire, and many Germans felt the treaty was unfair.

items.erreur_markdown: "Germany lost all its colonies when they became independent after 1919."
items.pourquoi_faux: The colonies did not become independent. They were taken away and ruled as mandates by the victorious powers under League supervision.
items.correction_markdown: Write that the colonies were handed to Britain, France, Belgium and others as League of Nations mandates.

items.erreur_markdown: "The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1918, when the fighting stopped."
items.pourquoi_faux: The fighting stopped with an armistice in November 1918. The Treaty of Versailles was signed later, on 28 June 1919.
items.correction_markdown: Say that Germany was defeated in 1918 and then forced to accept the Treaty of Versailles in 1919.

items.pourquoi_faux: Bismarck left office in 1890, long before 1914. The question concerns how the breakdown of his system helped bring war.
items.correction_markdown: Explain that after his fall the alliance system he built was not maintained, and rival blocs formed.

items.erreur_markdown: In answer to 'what losses did Germany suffer', a student describes the causes of the war.
items.pourquoi_faux: The command asks for the results of the war for Germany, not its causes.
items.correction_markdown: List the losses by group: land, colonies, army and money.

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) Name the treaty signed in 1919 that ended the war with Germany.
(b) State **one** limit placed on the German army by this treaty.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The **Treaty of Versailles**.
(b) For example: an army limited to **100,000 men**, or no tanks, or no military aircraft.

Award one mark for each correct answer.

items.enonce_markdown: Explain **two** ways in which the end of German rule affected Cameroon. [4 marks]
items.solution_markdown:
Way 1: Cameroon was divided between Britain and France, so the territory was split into two parts with different administrations and languages. Way 2: it became a League of Nations mandate, so Britain and France were supervised by an international body rather than ruling it as a private possession.

Award one mark for each way and one mark for each explanation. Total: **4 marks**.

items.enonce_markdown: "The collapse of Bismarck's system was the main cause of the First World War." To what extent do you agree? [10 marks]
items.solution_markdown:
For: after 1890 the Russian treaty lapsed, Russia and France allied, Britain joined France and Russia in the Entente, and Europe was split into two armed blocs. Against: the naval race, the Moroccan and Balkan crises, nationalism, and the assassination at Sarajevo in 1914 were also important. Judgement: the collapse of Bismarck's system created the setting for a general war, but the decisions made in 1914 and the earlier naval and colonial rivalry were also needed. So it was **an important long-term cause but not the only one**.

Award marks for knowledge (4), explanation (4) and a judgement (2).

items_markdown: The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919; Germany was not allowed to negotiate.
Losses: land in Europe, all colonies, armed forces, reparations and the war guilt clause.
Cameroon was divided between Britain and France and ruled as a League of Nations mandate.
After Bismarck left office in 1890, the alliance system changed, and Europe divided into the Triple Alliance and the Triple Entente.
For 'what losses', group them under four headings; for 'in what ways', give a chain of causes ending at Sarajevo.
